summary.text: The starry sky itself and first lord of the cosmos, born of Gaia to cover her on every side, and unmanned by his own son Cronus.

story.text: Gaia first bore starry Uranus, equal to herself, to cover her on every side and to be a sure seat for the blessed gods forever. By her he fathered the Titans, the Cyclopes and the Hundred-Handers — and hating his own children, he hid them away in the depths of the earth.

Gaia, groaning under the weight, forged a great sickle of adamant and asked her sons for vengeance. Only Cronus dared. From ambush he reaped his father's manhood and flung it into the sea; from the blood that fell on the earth came the Furies and the Giants, and from the foam upon the waves, Aphrodite.
